en: The Jātaka:
The Collection of Fours,
Chapter on the House-Spoiler (Kuṭidūsakavagga)
10. The Sīlavīmaṁsajātaka “Virtue alone, it is said, is beautiful;
virtue is unsurpassed in the world.”
“Behold the serpent of terrible venom;
though he be virtuous, he is not killed.
“As long as he has anything at all...”
Even then they did not devour him;
for when falcons gather in the world,
they do not harm one who possesses nothing.
One who is free from hope sleeps happily;
a fruitful hope is happy;
having turned hope into hopelessness—
Piṅgalā sleeps in peace;
there is nothing superior to concentration in this world or in the next.
“Being composed, he harms neither another nor himself.
The *Sīlavīmaṃsajātaka*, the tenth.
The third chapter is the Kuṭidūsakavagga.
Its summary (uddāna) is:
Samana, sadda, dūbha, and yācanaka.
Then there was Meṇḍaka, the most excellent of householders; then Godha, the best of those who shake their bodies; then Kālasumana, the foremost of those with beautiful hair;
and then Rādha, the most virtuous among the ten.
